newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev falls to 810-815 per dollar at close.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev falls to 810-815 per dollar at close.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 810-815 per dollar at the close from 805-810 in the morning and 768-770 at Tuesday's close due to higher demand for hard currency and increased lev liquidity, dealers said.
"A dollar purchase order from an oil importer pressured the lev in early trade. Pressure rose further when banks received fresh levs from treasury paper payments," said a dealer.

Foreign currency supply was low throughout the day due to the general reluctance of banks to offer foreign currency amid the ongoing rapid lev depreciation, traders said. Banks received some 28 billion levs in maturity payments on government securities on Wednesday and part of the payments were channelled to the interbank forex market, traders said.
The finance ministry drained part of the fresh liquidity inflow, selling one-week and four-week discount T-bills with a total par of 16.7 billion levs.

Traders said they expected the lev to lose another 10 to 20 to the dollar on Thursday amid the current political deadlock that has prevented formation of a new government. The lev traded at 575-585 at the beginning of the year. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
